mechanism_narrative: The recent step-down in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects weaker weekday circulation that suppresses spontaneous shopping trips and mall visits. If these series stay below their prior four-week levels, RETAIL_REC should remain lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not recover from their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises while RETAIL_REC stays depressed, households are substituting home-based activity for discretionary shopping, which delays retail visits for roughly one to two weeks. This should keep RETAIL_REC weak until RESIDENTIAL eases.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 15 points and RETAIL_REC stays below -30 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds above its prior 4-week mean within 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying elevated above 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: A joint decline in PARKS and TRANSIT signals broad reductions in out-of-home trips, which should spill over into retail and recreation with a one-week lag. If both remain weak together, RETAIL_REC should fall further over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days even though PARKS and TRANSIT both remain below their last-4-week averages.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops sharply from one week to the next, the same shock will reduce access to retail corridors and lower RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks. The effect is strongest when WORKPLACES is also falling, indicating a broader mobility restriction or commuting contraction.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week from its current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days after a week-on-week TRANSIT drop greater than 3 points, especially when WORKPLACES also falls.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM often precedes broader neighborhood shopping trips and can partially lift retail footfall after about two weeks. If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising from its current level, RETAIL_REC should edge upward.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise from the current snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL indicates more local, low-distance activity and time spent near home, which crowds out discretionary retail trips. Over four weeks this pattern should push RETAIL_REC lower relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both remain elevated versus baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS recovers sharply from a depressed level, it signals better weather or seasonal outdoor substitution that can raise overall mobility and retail outings within one week. A continuing improvement in PARKS should therefore lift RETAIL_REC quickly.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week from a negative level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days after PARKS improves by at least 5 points from a negative weekly level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained combination of low TRANSIT and low WORKPLACES indicates commuting suppression that directly depresses weekday retail demand. If both remain below their current four-week means, RETAIL_REC should stay below the prior four-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below their current four-week means.
